checking_content:
Loading screen and reveal
Preconditions: Page just opened.
Steps:
  1. Observe the initial overlay and wait for it to disappear. -> expected: A full-viewport black overlay with a centered spinning blue-border circle is shown, then fades out smoothly after the Earth texture loads, revealing the globe and HUD.
Pass: Loading overlay with animated spinner is displayed first and fades away cleanly without blocking interaction afterwards.
expected_result: Loading overlay with animated spinner is displayed first and fades away cleanly without blocking interaction afterwards.

checking_content:
Earth globe, atmosphere and starfield
Preconditions: Loading finished.
Steps:
  1. Observe the scene. -> expected: A photorealistic Earth sphere with a world-map texture is surrounded by a glowing blue atmospheric rim, over a dark space background with many stars.
Pass: Textured globe, blue atmosphere glow, and a starry background are all visible and cleanly rendered.
expected_result: Textured globe, blue atmosphere glow, and a starry background are all visible and cleanly rendered.

checking_content:
Flight arcs and aircraft animation
Preconditions: Loading finished, flights visible.
Steps:
  1. Watch the globe for a few seconds. -> expected: Many colored flight-path arcs span between cities, and small airplane icons/particles move smoothly along those arcs.
Pass: Multiple colored arcs are rendered and aircraft visibly progress along them without stuttering or popping.
expected_result: Multiple colored arcs are rendered and aircraft visibly progress along them without stuttering or popping.

checking_content:
Orbit and zoom interaction
Preconditions: Scene fully loaded.
Steps:
  1. Drag on the globe, then scroll to zoom in and out. -> expected: Dragging rotates the globe smoothly with inertia; zooming is limited so the camera never clips through the Earth surface or flies absurdly far away.
Pass: Rotate and zoom both work continuously and the globe remains interactive afterwards.
expected_result: Rotate and zoom both work continuously and the globe remains interactive afterwards.

checking_content:
Control panel with flight parameters
Preconditions: HUD revealed after loading.
Steps:
  1. Open/inspect the top-right control panel and change a flight-related parameter (e.g. flight count, animation speed, plane size). -> expected: A dat.GUI-style panel with groups such as Plane, Animation, Flight, Lighting and Brightness exists, and changing values visibly affects the scene.
Pass: Panel is present with the described control groups and at least one change produces a visible scene update.
expected_result: Panel is present with the described control groups and at least one change produces a visible scene update.

checking_content:
Show/hide toggles and lighting effects
Preconditions: Control panel visible.
Steps:
  1. Toggle 'show paths' or 'show planes', then toggle the day/night or real-time sun lighting option. -> expected: Toggling paths/planes hides or reveals those elements; the lighting toggle switches the globe between day and night shading.
Pass: Each toggle produces the corresponding visual change in the scene.
expected_result: Each toggle produces the corresponding visual change in the scene.

checking_content:
FPS counter overlay
Preconditions: Loading finished.
Steps:
  1. Look at the top-left corner. -> expected: A small FPS monitor panel is displayed and its value fluctuates with rendering.
Pass: FPS counter is visible after load and shows a plausible changing value.
expected_result: FPS counter is visible after load and shows a plausible changing value.

checking_content:
Footer attribution and live coordinates
Preconditions: HUD revealed.
Steps:
  1. Inspect the bottom bar, then rotate the globe. -> expected: The footer shows an attribution link on the left (GitHub author credit) and a live latitude/longitude readout on the right that updates as the camera moves.
Pass: Footer link is present and the coordinate readout changes while orbiting the globe.
expected_result: Footer link is present and the coordinate readout changes while orbiting the globe.

checking_content:
Startup camera intro
Preconditions: Page freshly loaded.
Steps:
  1. Observe the camera right after the loading screen fades. -> expected: The camera performs a short cinematic ease-in (smoothly settling from a slightly farther distance toward the globe) before resting in the default orbit position.
Pass: A smooth animated camera transition is visible at startup instead of an abrupt static framing.
expected_result: A smooth animated camera transition is visible at startup instead of an abrupt static framing.
